quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check if any vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also make sure no other drivers are moving into the same spot from a different direction.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Interstate driving requires you to stay alert and drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers making a left turn must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: It is dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely because:

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
They brake more slowly than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than cars. If you follow too closely, you may crash into them if they stop suddenly. You need enough space and time to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When someone is tailgating you, create more space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a crash.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is both a solid and dashed yellow line, only the traffic next to the dashed line can cross the center line to pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive at least 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. The speed advisory sign shows the safe speed to use for the upcoming curve.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and smoothly.
Drive the same way you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers' signals and instructions. Flaggers are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: Clear all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your vehicle's windows and mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Has no effect on your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol level nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle means:

options.text: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
It is an ambulance.
It is a school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This orange triangle means the vehicle moves at 25 mph or slower. You may see it on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn carriages.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed at this location. You must obey this sign.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn after slowing down and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn until the light turns green.
May turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn on a red arrow.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.
Where signs and road markings allow passing.
Around a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Do not pass around curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming vehicles. Only pass where signs and road markings permit it, and only when you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: This black and yellow sign means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to construction.
The road ahead turns sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangerous conditions ahead. This sign warns you to slow down because the road turns sharply.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: Only look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and left shoulder for left lane changes.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and left shoulder for left lane changes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass.

questions.question: What should drivers use to see better in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: What should you do if oncoming headlights are blinding you at night?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your car on the road safely until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Passing is permitted from the left.
Passing is permitted from the right.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. They mean no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: What should you do because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Make constant visual checks.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make constant visual checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: Which action blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision scene.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision scene.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at collisions causes traffic jams. Avoid this and keep moving at normal speed.
